editorial:
Even after Jigsaw dies, his games keep going, and this time Lieutenant Rigg gets pulled in to save two colleagues. You follow a stressed cop racing through brutal traps while flashbacks reveal more about Jigsaw and his helper. The movie feels dark, tense, and fast, with lots of blood and puzzle pieces. You also see how Jigsaw's rules push people to make ugly choices. If you like crime stories mixed with horror, you will find plenty to chew on here.

The acting is solid, especially from the leads, and the pacing rarely slows down. The traps are nasty and creative, though the story can feel crowded with too many twists. Some scenes are hard to watch, so skip it if gore bothers you. Fans of the series should enjoy the backstory and surprises. The ending ties back to earlier clues, so pay attention. Watch it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Rigg reaches the last room and learns the game was never about saving his colleagues the way he thought. Jigsaw's plan connects to Hoffman and the bigger picture, and Rigg's own choices become part of the trap. The twist shows that Jigsaw's death did not stop his work, and someone close is carrying it on. The movie ends with a shocking reveal that sets up more danger ahead.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves horror thrillers with twists and traps.
